London
January 14, 1998
Orange County Prosecutes Cannabis Club Founder In Face of Overwhelming Public Opinion (Notice a Pattern?)
Britain's Labor government Wednesday ignored overwhelming public opposition to the criminalization of medical cannabis users and said that it would continue to support a ban that began only 27 years ago. Home Affairs junior minister Paul Boateng told Parliament that ``To allow any substance -- not just cannabis -- to be prescribed (by a doctor) without adequate proof of its effectiveness and safety would be a highly irresponsible and retrograde step.''

He did not cite any research on the therapeutic benefits of arresting the sick and dying. The fact that the public overwhelming opposes this policy demonstrates the high political stakes. As in America, the prohibitionist establishment realizes that having cannabis used under medical supervision would make the continuation of "reefer madness" impossible. Consequently, they are willing to pay the consequences of trying  to suppress it. This makes the end more likely to come all at once, with a great embarrassment to the government.
